text: The decisive sentence in Genesis 6 concerns God's inner life. Yahweh sees "that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually," and "it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart" (Genesis 6:5–6). The grief comes before the sentence of judgment and gives that sentence its character. A maker's sorrow over what his creatures have become drives the flood. Before any rain falls, the first covenant in Scripture appears: "But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee" (6:18). The promise reaches past Noah to the animals, "two of every sort" (6:19), and to the food that will keep them all alive: "it shall be for food for thee, and for them" (6:21). In the same chapter where God announces "the end of all flesh" (6:13), he also arranges, in detail, what will survive it. Noah, the one man who "found grace in the eyes of the LORD" (6:8), is told to gather in the creatures God is about to drown.
